passages.text: Then I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, “Go, pour out on the earth the seven bowls of God’s wrath.”
passages.sermon:
A loud voice spoke from the temple.
I heard this voice.
The voice spoke to the seven angels.
The voice gave a command.
The voice said, “Go.”
The voice said, “Pour out the seven bowls.”
These bowls hold the wrath of God.
God’s wrath must be poured out on the earth.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα μεγάλης φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ λεγούσης τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις Ὑπάγετε καὶ ἐκχέετε τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν

passages.text: So the first angel went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and loathsome, malignant sores broke out on those who had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image.
passages.sermon:
The first angel acted.
The first angel went out.
The first angel poured out his bowl on the earth.
Sores appeared.
The sores were evil and painful.
These sores came upon certain people.
These people had the mark of the beast.
These people worshiped the image of the beast.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν καὶ ἐγένετο ἕλκος κακὸν καὶ πονηρὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ἔχοντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And the second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and it turned to blood like that of the dead, and every living thing in the sea died.
passages.sermon:
The second angel acted.
The second angel held a bowl of God's wrath.
The second angel poured his bowl into the sea.
The sea changed.
The sea became blood.
The blood was like the blood of a dead person.
Every living thing in the sea died.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα ὡς νεκροῦ καὶ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ζωῆς ἀπέθανεν τὰ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ

passages.text: And the third angel poured out his bowl into the rivers and springs of water, and they turned to blood.
passages.sermon:
The third angel acted.
The third angel held a bowl.
The third angel poured his bowl into the rivers.
The third angel poured his bowl into the springs of water.
The rivers turned to blood.
The springs of water turned to blood.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς ποταμοὺς καὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα

passages.text: And I heard the angel of the waters say: “Righteous are You, O Holy One, who is and was, because You have brought these judgments.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the waters spoke.
I heard the angel speak.
The angel said these words to God.
God is righteous.
God is holy.
God exists now.
God existed in the past.
God made these judgments.
God is righteous because He made these judgments.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῶν ὑδάτων λέγοντος Δίκαιος εἶ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν ὁ Ὅσιος ὅτι ταῦτα ἔκρινας

passages.text: For they have spilled the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink, as they deserve.”
passages.sermon:
Some people killed saints.
Some people killed prophets.
You gave these people blood to drink.
They deserve this.
passages.original: ὅτι αἷμα ἁγίων καὶ προφητῶν ἐξέχεαν καὶ αἷμα αὐτοῖς δέδωκας πιεῖν ἄξιοί εἰσιν

passages.text: And I heard the altar reply: “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are Your judgments.”
passages.sermon:
The altar spoke.
The altar said, “Yes, Lord God Almighty.”
The Lord God is all-powerful.
The altar said, “Your judgments are true.”
The altar said, “Your judgments are just.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου λέγοντος Ναί Κύριε ὁ Θεός ὁ Παντοκράτωρ ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις σου

passages.text: Then the fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was given power to scorch the people with fire.
passages.sermon:
The fourth angel acted.
The fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun.
The sun received power.
The sun had power to scorch people with fire.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἥλιον καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ καυματίσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐν πυρί

passages.text: And the people were scorched by intense heat, and they cursed the name of God, who had authority over these plagues; yet they did not repent and give Him glory.
passages.sermon:
God has authority over these plagues.
The people suffered great heat.
The heat scorched them.
They cursed the name of God.
They did not repent.
They did not give God glory.
passages.original: καὶ ἐκαυματίσθησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι καῦμα μέγα καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ἔχοντος τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τὰς πληγὰς ταύτας καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν δοῦναι αὐτῷ δόξαν

passages.text: And the fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was plunged into darkness, and men began to gnaw their tongues in anguish and curse the God of heaven for their pains and sores; yet they did not repent of their deeds.
passages.sermon:
The fifth angel acted.
The fifth angel poured out his bowl.
He poured it on the throne of the beast.
The beast ruled a kingdom.
The kingdom became dark.
People suffered great pain.
People chewed their tongues because of pain.
People had sores.
People cursed the God of heaven because of their pain and sores.
They did not repent of their deeds.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ἐσκοτωμένη καὶ ἐμασῶντο τὰς γλώσσας αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πόνου καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸν Θεὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκ τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑλκῶν αὐτῶν καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν

passages.text: And the sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up to prepare the way for the kings of the East.
passages.sermon:
The sixth angel acted.
The sixth angel poured out his bowl.
He poured it on the great river Euphrates.
The water of the river dried up.
This prepared a way.
The way was for the kings from the east.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν μέγαν τὸν Εὐφράτην καὶ ἐξηράνθη τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ ἵνα ἑτοιμασθῇ ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν βασιλέων τῶν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου

passages.text: And I saw three unclean spirits that looked like frogs coming out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet.
passages.sermon:
John saw three unclean spirits.
These spirits looked like frogs.
The spirits came out of the mouth of the dragon.
The spirits came out of the mouth of the beast.
The spirits came out of the mouth of the false prophet.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ δράκοντος καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ ψευδοπροφήτου πνεύματα τρία ἀκάθαρτα ὡς βάτραχοι

passages.text: These are demonic spirits that perform signs and go out to all the kings of the earth, to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty.
passages.sermon:
These spirits are demons.
They perform miraculous signs.
They go out to all the kings of the earth.
They gather the kings together.
They prepare the kings for battle.
This battle will happen on the great day of God the Almighty.
passages.original: εἰσὶν γὰρ πνεύματα δαιμονίων ποιοῦντα σημεῖα ἃ ἐκπορεύεται ἐπὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Παντοκράτορος

passages.text: “Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed, so that he will not go naked and let his shame be exposed.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks.
Jesus says, “I am coming suddenly.
I will come when people do not expect me.
A thief comes without warning.
I will come in the same way.
A person is blessed if he stays awake.
A person is blessed if he keeps his clothes on.
If a person does not stay awake, he may be caught unprepared.
If a person does not keep his clothes, he may walk around naked.
If he is naked, others will see his shame.”
passages.original: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ὡς κλέπτης μακάριος ὁ γρηγορῶν καὶ τηρῶν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἵνα μὴ γυμνὸς περιπατῇ καὶ βλέπωσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.
passages.sermon: Demonic spirits gathered the kings.\r\nThey brought the kings to a place.\r\nThis place is called Armageddon in Hebrew.
passages.original: Καὶ συνήγαγεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἁρ¦μαγεδών

passages.text: Then the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came from the throne in the temple, saying, “It is done!”
passages.sermon:
The seventh angel acted.
He poured out his bowl into the air.
A loud voice spoke from the temple.
The voice came from the throne.
The voice said, “It is done!”
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀέρα καὶ ἐξῆλθεν φωνὴ μεγάλη ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου λέγουσα Γέγονεν

passages.text: And there were flashes of lightning, and rumblings, and peals of thunder, and a great earthquake the likes of which had not occurred since men were upon the earth—so mighty was the great quake.
passages.sermon:
God sent signs and judgments upon the earth.
Flashes of lightning appeared.
Loud sounds filled the air.
Thunder rolled across the sky.
A great earthquake shook the land.
This earthquake was greater than any before.
No earthquake like this had happened since people first lived on earth.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί καὶ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας οἷος οὐκ ἐγένετο ἀφ’ οὗ ἄνθρωπος ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τηλικοῦτος σεισμὸς οὕτω μέγας

passages.text: The great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations collapsed. And God remembered Babylon the great and gave her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath.
passages.sermon:
God acted in judgment.
God split the great city into three parts.
The cities of the nations collapsed.
God remembered Babylon the great.
God gave Babylon the cup filled with the wine of the fury of His wrath.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη εἰς τρία μέρη καὶ αἱ πόλεις τῶν ἐθνῶν ἔπεσαν καὶ Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη ἐμνήσθη ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ δοῦναι αὐτῇ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then every island fled, and no mountain could be found.
passages.sermon: Every island disappeared.\r\nNo mountain remained.\r\nPeople could not find any mountain.
passages.original: Καὶ πᾶσα νῆσος ἔφυγεν καὶ ὄρη οὐχ εὑρέθησαν

passages.text: And great hailstones weighing almost a hundred pounds each rained down on them from above. And men cursed God for the plague of hail, because it was so horrendous.
passages.sermon:
God sent a terrible plague of hail.
The hailstones were very large.
Each hailstone weighed almost a hundred pounds.
The hailstones fell from the sky onto people.
The people suffered greatly from the hail.
The plague of hail was extremely severe.
The people cursed God because of the hail.
passages.original: καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη ὡς ταλαντιαία καταβαίνει ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν Θεὸν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς τῆς χαλάζης ὅτι μεγάλη ἐστὶν ἡ πληγὴ αὐτῆς σφόδρα
